question: How does Grieg’s own pacing shape the shared opening?
intro: Grieg recorded this shortened version of his own piano piece in Paris in 1903. Its two-minute disc is not the complete score, and the comparison follows only shared opening material rather than equating whole-file durations.

sections.mNote: The complete historical disc, not the complete score

cues.title: A disc, not a roll
cues.text: This is Grieg’s own acoustic disc, recorded in Paris on 2 May 1903, not a piano-roll reconstruction. Listen to the relationship between melody and accompaniment, while remembering that the horn and transfer limit what survives of his touch.
cues.evidence: Marston’s discography lists the session, Wedding-Day at Troldhaugen and matrix 2149F: https://www.marstonrecords.com/products/legendary-piano. The streamed Commons transfer is separate from Marston’s restoration.

cues.title: The shared opening passage
cues.text: The comparison begins eighteen seconds into this side and stops at 1:28. Within that shared passage, compare the spacing of the piano attacks with Vetter’s complete performance; do not infer Grieg’s tempo from the two recordings’ total durations.
cues.evidence: The analysis locates an early boundary near 0:16. The final map uses only Grieg 18–88 seconds and Vetter 21.6–116.31 seconds; the cut ending and Vetter’s contrasting middle are excluded.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Pitch is not harmony
cues.text: The old recording’s unstable pitch and restricted sound can obscure the harmony. Keep the melody’s direction in view rather than treating every wavering tone as an expressive inflection or a different written note.
cues.evidence: Marston’s notes discuss the early Paris discs’ pitch instability and uncertain replay speed. This report’s weak global key estimate is not used to reinterpret the score; no exact tuning is asserted.

cues.title: A stronger recorded presence
cues.text: Across this middle stretch, the piano gains recorded level. Compare the continuity of the pulse with the growth in sound: stronger attacks and a faster beat are different things.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/grieg-wedding-day-grieg-1903.txt: measured changes at 0:46 and 0:52; level rises from −16.9 dB at 0:45 to −9.2 dB at 0:55. The report does not establish a beat-by-beat tempo.

cues.title: Across the later crest
cues.text: This later span carries some of the side’s highest recorded levels. Follow the shape of the phrase through the crest; the automatic match becomes unreliable near the abbreviated ending, so the comparison stops before it.
cues.evidence: The strongest measured boundary is 1:14; 1:15, 1:25 and 1:30 are among the loudest windows. An exploratory map stalled around 1:30, so its final section was excluded rather than presented as a tempo change.

cues.title: The shortened side closes
cues.text: The recording recedes towards its ending. This closing material is not mapped onto Vetter’s complete performance: the two-minute disc omits much of the score, and a convincing comparison must leave that difference audible.
cues.evidence: The report falls from −13.5 dB at 1:35 through −21.1 at 1:45 to −49.4 at 2:00. The complete source file is played, while alignment is restricted to 18–88 seconds.

fields.label: Work version
fields.value: Abridged solo-piano performance by the composer
fields.note: The complete 1903 disc is streamed, not a digitally assembled excerpt. Its approximately two-minute duration is not the complete score. Comparison alignment excludes the shortened ending and music found only in Vetter’s complete reading.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: Commons identifies 1903 in the description; its 10 March 2012 Date field is the upload date.

fields.label: Catalogue
fields.note: IMSLP lists No. 3800; Marston lists 35515. The exact pressing used for the Commons transfer is not identified.

fields.label: Matrix, take, sides
fields.note: No take suffix is supplied by these sources.

fields.label: Transfer
fields.note: The uploader is not identified as the transfer engineer. The Commons description “Original tape” does not establish the 1903 medium or a transfer chain.

fields.label: Transfer date
fields.note: 10 March 2012 is the upload date, not a demonstrated transfer date.

fields.label: Processing
fields.note: The Commons transfer’s restoration and replay speed are not documented. Marston discusses pitch instability in these early discs, but its modern restoration is not the audio streamed here.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Underlying piano composition is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms
fields.note: Grieg died in 1907. This does not establish rights in a modern edition.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.value: US public domain: sound recording first published in 1903
fields.note: IMSLP’s recording entry names Gramophone & Typewriter No. 3800, 1903, matrix 2149F; Marston corroborates matrix, pianist and 2 May 1903 session. The recording’s pre-1926 publication, not Commons’ composition-only PD-old tag, is the basis. No non-commercial restriction appears in the inspected source entry.
